passages.title: A Book About Life, Not Death
passages.body: Tuesdays with Morrie is one of the most loved books about life ever written. Its author, Mitch Albom, was a busy sports journalist who felt that something was missing from his days. Everything changed when he was reunited with his favourite college professor, Morrie Schwartz. On learning that Morrie was being weakened by a severe illness, Mitch began visiting him every Tuesday. During these weekly talks, many lessons on the meaning of life were shared between the two friends. Although the book is about dying, it is not pessimistic at all. Instead, it is filled with joy and hope. Morrie's bravery near the end of his life has been described as inspirational, and it has encouraged countless readers to value their own lives more. Far from being a sad story about death, it gently reminds us that once we learn how to die, we finally learn how to live.

questions.stem: What was Mitch Albom's job before he met Morrie again?
questions.explanation: 原文 'a busy sports journalist' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why did Mitch start visiting Morrie every Tuesday?
options: Because Morrie had offered him money.
Because Morrie had become seriously ill.
Because Mitch had lost his job.
questions.explanation: 原文 'was being weakened by a severe illness' 的转述。

questions.stem: What does the writer say the book is really about?
questions.explanation: 末句 'once we learn how to die, we finally learn how to live' 的转述。

passages.title: Who Was Morrie Schwartz?
passages.body: Morrie Schwartz was loved by his students long before he became known around the world. For many years he had taught at a university, where his lessons were remembered not only for their clever ideas but also for their warmth. When a severe illness slowly took away his strength, Morrie was not filled with despair. He chose instead to share what he had learned about love, work and friendship. From his window, each change of season was observed by him as though through new eyes, and ordinary things seemed more beautiful than ever before. His former student Mitch wrote down their conversations so that the old teacher's wisdom could be passed on. In this way, the quiet courage of one dying professor has been turned into a message of hope. Today that message is read by millions of people in many different countries.

questions.stem: How were Morrie's university lessons remembered?
options: For both their ideas and their warmth.
questions.explanation: 原文 'remembered not only for their clever ideas but also for their warmth' 的转述。

questions.stem: How did Morrie react to his illness?
options: He hid himself away in despair.
He shared what he had learned instead of giving up.
questions.explanation: 原文 'chose instead to share what he had learned' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why did Mitch write down their talks?
options: So that he could become a sports star.
So that he could sell the old house.
So that he could forget his teacher.
So that Morrie's wisdom could reach others.
questions.explanation: 原文 'so that the old teacher's wisdom could be passed on' 的转述。

passages.title: The Big Things in Life
passages.body: One of the strongest messages in Tuesdays with Morrie is about the so-called 'big things' in life. According to Morrie, how we think and what we value should be chosen by ourselves, and never be decided for us by any society. While we are living, we are easily distracted by smaller matters, such as gathering material possessions. Yet money, Morrie warns, will not always make people happy, and looking different from others does not make a person abnormal. Readers are encouraged to find out for themselves what truly matters and to build their own values around love and honest communication. Many who finish the book say they feel as if they have been woken from a long sleep. Their eyes are opened to the world, and small daily worries are suddenly seen as far less important than simple kindness.

questions.stem: According to Morrie, who should decide your values?
options: Society should decide them for you.
questions.explanation: 原文 'should be chosen by ourselves' 的转述。

questions.stem: What does Morrie say about money?
options: It is the most important thing of all.
It does not always bring happiness.
It should always be hidden away.
questions.explanation: 原文 'money… will not always make people happy' 的转述。

questions.stem: How do many readers feel after finishing the book?
options: Suddenly more awake and aware of life.
Sorry that they ever read it.
questions.explanation: 原文 'as if they have been woken from a long sleep' 的转述。

passages.title: Wisdom in Old Stories
passages.body: Long before printed books existed, wisdom was passed on through storytelling. One of the earliest collections of such stories is Aesop's Fables, which history credits to a Greek storyteller named Aesop. It is believed that he lived in ancient Greece more than two thousand years ago. Most of the characters in his tales are animals, whose qualities were cleverly used by Aesop to reflect human nature. At the end of each fable, a short lesson, known as a moral, is given in a single memorable phrase. Because these morals are simple and true, they have never been forgotten. Today, Aesop's Fables are still enjoyed by both children and adults all over the world. The stories remind us that important truths can be found even in the shortest of tales, and that lessons about life are often best remembered when they are wrapped inside a good story.

questions.stem: How was wisdom shared before printed books existed?
questions.explanation: 原文 'wisdom was passed on through storytelling' 的转述。

questions.stem: Why did Aesop use animals in his stories?
questions.explanation: 原文 'used by Aesop to reflect human nature' 的转述。

questions.stem: What is a 'moral' in one of Aesop's fables?
options: The full name of the writer.
A short lesson at the end of the story.
A long introduction to the tale.
A list of all the animals.
questions.explanation: 原文 'a short lesson, known as a moral' 的转述。

passages.title: Searching for the Blue Bird
passages.body: The Blue Bird is a famous play in which two children, Tyltyl and Mytyl, are sent by a fairy to search for the Blue Bird of Happiness. Their long adventure takes them through many magical places, yet the bird they are looking for is never quite caught. Only when the tired children return home is the truth finally understood: the Blue Bird had been there all the time. Happiness, the play suggests, is not to be found in luxury or wealth, but in simple things such as family life and acts of kindness. Near the end, the bird is given to a sick neighbour's daughter, and the little girl is suddenly cured. Then, in a surprising moment, the bird escapes and flies away, and the audience is asked to help find it again. Through this gentle ending, we are reminded that happiness must always be searched for and shared.

questions.stem: What are the two children sent to look for?
options: A magical bird that stands for happiness.
questions.explanation: 原文 'search for the Blue Bird of Happiness' 的转述。

questions.stem: Where does the play say happiness is found?
options: In simple things like family and kindness.
questions.explanation: 原文 'in simple things such as family life and acts of kindness' 的转述。

questions.stem: What happens to the bird at the very end?
options: It flies away and must be found again.
It is sold at a busy market.
It turns into a piece of gold.
It is locked in a cage forever.
questions.explanation: 原文 'the bird escapes and flies away… asked to help find it again' 的转述。

passages.title: Never Too Late to Learn
passages.body: Age, as one remarkable story shows, need not be a barrier to learning. Many years ago, a woman named Janet had to leave university before finishing her degree, because her family came first. The dream of graduating, however, was never completely given up. When her children had grown, she returned to study, even though at first she felt nervous among classmates who were far younger than she was. Her courage was soon rewarded. After several years of hard work, she finally graduated, and her happy story was reported in the local news. Today, more and more older students are being welcomed by universities, and in some countries no upper age limit is set at all. Janet's advice to others is simple: it is never too late to start again. A goal that is truly worth reaching, she believes, should be followed at any age.

questions.stem: Why did Janet first leave university?
options: Her family had to come first.
She had no money for books.
questions.explanation: 原文 'because her family came first' 的转述。

questions.stem: How did Janet feel when she returned to study?
questions.explanation: 原文 'felt nervous among classmates who were far younger' 的转述。

questions.stem: What is Janet's advice to other people?
options: Only the young should ever study.
Give up quickly if learning is hard.
You can always begin again, whatever your age.
questions.explanation: 原文 'it is never too late to start again' 的转述。
